content:
Last month, OpenAI teased a hardware product to be sold under the Codex brand. Today the company officially unveiled the result of a collaboration with Work Louder: a $230 Codex Micro keyboard.

Here is the product description:

The keyboard comes in two versions: tactile (clicky) and silent.

Per the website: "Each Agent key shows RGB lighting based on Codex's real-time status, so you can see at a glance which one is thinking, running, waiting, or done — then switch conversations."

The product page also lists three Codex-specific features:

  • Instant Skill Triggers: A flick of the joystick launches common Codex workflows, like reviewing PRs, debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Core actions at your fingertips: The command key gives you dedicated shortcuts for the actions you use most: accept, reject, chat, new chat. Less switching. More shipping.
  • Adjust compute intensity: Twist the dial to change the reasoning level on the fly. Stay efficient on simple tasks, and turn it up when you need deeper thinking.

That's about it. It's been quite a month for OpenAI and hardware.
